key_insight: The paper demonstrates the first bulk synthesis of phase-pure Cs2AgBiI6, showing that careful moisture control enables complete halide exchange from the bromide precursor.
engineering_relevance: This establishes a new lead-free iodide double-perovskite candidate with visible-light absorption, film processability, and photoconductive response for solar and optoelectronic devices.
method: Prepared Cs2AgBiI6 microcrystals by anion exchange from phase-pure Cs2AgBiBr6.
Eliminated trace moisture in the bromide precursor to enable full iodide conversion and phase purity.
Extended the approach to thin films via flash thermal evaporation followed by anion exchange.
evidence_signal: The resulting material showed a 1.70 ± 0.05 eV optical bandgap, near-infrared photoluminescence at 1.03 eV, months-long stability in inert atmosphere, and measurable photoconductivity in films.
watch_item: The synthesis depends sensitively on removing trace moisture, so reproducibility and scale-up may be challenging under less controlled processing conditions.
paper_title: Synthesis of the Elusive Bulk Iodide Double-Perovskite Semiconductor, Cs2AgBiI6: Microcrystals and Photoconductive Films
